requires: Python is one of the explicitly supported CPython versions.
The command is executed from, or can discover, the repository root.
The selected profile is one of status, runtime, core, solver, docs, or release.
Network access is required only by bootstrap and clean-install operations.
ensures: Local and CI callers dispatch through the same repository-owned Python entry point.
Every profile has an explicit dependency set, command set, platform policy, and timeout budget.
The status profile uses only the Python standard library and never installs dependencies.
The runtime profile installs the base wheel or editable package without development dependencies.
The core profile installs base plus dev dependencies and never imports python-sat.
The solver profile installs base, dev, and solvers and is supported only where compatible wheels exist.
The docs profile includes the pinned documentation toolchain.
The release profile builds artifacts, installs the wheel into a clean environment, and runs smoke checks.
A missing, incompatible, skipped, timed-out, or failing required command returns a nonzero exit status.
Human and JSON summaries identify the profile, commands, results, platform, and interpreter without claiming unrun checks.
raises: No Python exception crosses the CLI boundary for an expected validation failure.
Programmer defects may produce a diagnostic traceback only in explicit debug mode.

effects.filesystem: bootstrap may create or modify only the selected environment and standard build/test artifacts; check operations are read-only except tool-owned caches
effects.process: may execute Python, pip, build, ruff, pytest, twine, and documented smoke subprocesses with bounded timeouts
effects.network: bootstrap may contact configured package indexes; check operations do not require network
effects.repository: never edits PLAN, TODO, PROGRESS, accepted contracts, or product source

determinism.dependency_resolution: constraints.txt and explicitly pinned toolchain requirements define the tested set
determinism.output: UTF-8 with stable reason codes; elapsed time and absolute paths are noncanonical diagnostics
determinism.platform_variation: unsupported optional backends are explicit profile refusals, not silent skips

budget.cancellation: terminate the active child process and return a distinct interrupted result

epistemics.passed: every required command in the selected profile returned success
epistemics.failed: at least one required command returned nonzero
epistemics.unsupported: the selected profile is incompatible with the current platform or interpreter
epistemics.timed_out: a required command exceeded its declared budget
epistemics.not_run: the profile was described but not executed; never equivalent to passed

invariants: Profile names and meanings are stable within contract v1.
CI workflow commands call tools/dev.py rather than duplicating profile semantics.
The same constraints and profile definitions are used on Windows and Linux.
Core success never implies solver, docs, full-product, or release success.
No profile reports overall green while one of its required commands is red.
